decision.summaryForCoordinator: The sharpest test in this dispatch is the status token, and the trap behind it was real rather than hypothetical. DR-G25's own final register cell is a bare 'OPEN', which is what the subject carries. The row it names most often, DR-131, ends with 'Hard blocker for preview analyze; condition 2 SATISFIED-requiring per D-134' — so a join that took its token from the row it discusses rather than the row it belongs to would have imported a SATISFIED-requiring standing into a file whose entire purpose is to not SATISFY DR-131. It took the right one, live G25 v2 independently corroborates 'OPEN', and no live row in file 08 carries a bare SATISFIED status cell. Every carried phrase is == equal to live G25 v2: memberVerbatim 'missing-required-rung corpus (DR-131 NT-3)' — which also appears verbatim in the live register row, so harness, register and join agree — the two cell ids in order, and the single-limb list ['NT-3']. On the collapse prohibition I tested more than preservation: the two cells are a genuinely distinct pair on the live inputNamed text, one a rung absent while construction may still be possible and the other the universe unconstructible outright, which is why live v2 sets corpusTakesBothReadings true and says a fixture author must pin both. The subject keeps them as separate fields, repeats both inside the fixture obligation, and sets ntReadingsCollapsed false. I read D-151 and D-056 clause 5 in the coordinator record rather than accepting the paraphrases: D-151 says 'It owns DR-131 NT-3 only' and 'NT-3 leftover-design closes: remainder is G25 execution', and clause 5 says authoring fixtures and harness specifications remains lawful design work while execution remains qualification — the subject uses clause 5 to keep the fixture obligation open, not to close it. The row-local NT-3 claim was verified from the sibling's own bytes: g23-leftover-join.v1 has registerRow DR-G23 and DR-133 as its only DR row, while the subject contains zero DR-G23 tokens and five G25-scoped obligations. Partition is exact at five obligations, the single true flag is OBL-G25-FX-AUTHORING, all ten cited digests match, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head and live HEAD, required-now is 26 across thirty gate rows, artifact and version both say 1, and the subject did not move. Twenty-five attacks run, twenty-five refuted, zero findings. Two things a coordinator should know: D-151 also records that DR-131's NT-5 through NT-8 remain leftover-design, and they sit outside both this join and the G23 sibling — correct scoping for a DR-G25 join, but this file alone is not the whole DR-131 picture. And a disclosure that bears on weight: I REJECTED G25 harness v1 at CLAUDE-G25-V1-B1 for having no NT-3 corpus class, v2 repaired it by adding the two-cell structure, and the 'do not collapse' duty judged here is downstream of that repair. I re-derived every identifier from live v2 bytes rather than from my own reviews, and tested the split on its merits rather than assuming it was worth keeping.
